splits.random: GroupKFold(5) on ligand_main_fragment — the MSRS-2 protocol
splits.doi: GroupKFold(5) on doi — no paper in both train and test
splits.year: LeaveOneGroupOut on the year parsed from the DOI; years with < 100 rows pooled as 'early'

design.primary_metric: MAE in log10 units; delta sign accuracy at the MSRS-1 noise floor
design.decay_reference: the random split of the same endpoint, recomputed here
design.scope: all three splits hold out papers, years or scaffolds, never a metal; this validates interpolation only

caveats: Only 30.6% of potency rows (29.9% of cisplatin_ratio) carry a parseable year in the DOI, so the year cell is a subset and is not directly comparable in n.
The year split holds out whole papers by publication year, but a paper's DOI year can predate its print issue; treat the labels as approximate.
The DOI split still lets the same ligand appear in train and test under a different paper, which is realistic but not a chemistry holdout.
The scaffold split removes ring-system memorisation but keeps ligand decoration patterns; it is not a full analogue-series holdout.
No split holds out a metal. MSRS-4 covers that question and the answer there is negative.

The decision-utility block re-asks the MSRS-6 question on these splits but was not the pre-registered primary analysis; MSRS-6's kill criterion was fixed on the random split and is not reopened post hoc here.
